title: Custom Protocol Scheme Handlers
summary: Register custom protocols (app://, kromium://) to serve web assets from the classpath, local directories, or dynamic handlers.

sections.title: How Custom Schemes Work
sections.content:
Custom schemes allow you to intercept `app://myapp/index.html` style URLs and serve content from JVM resources, local files, or dynamically generated responses. This enables building fully offline desktop apps with web UIs.

**Two-step process:**
1. **Register the scheme** with `KromiumCustomScheme` in `KromiumConfig` (before engine init).
2. **Register the handler** via `engine.registerSchemeHandler(...)` (after engine init).

sections.title: Registering a Custom Scheme
sections.content: Custom schemes must be declared before engine initialization. Use `KromiumCustomScheme.secure()` for a secure scheme with CORS and Fetch API enabled, or construct with full control over security flags.

codeSnippet.code:
val config = KromiumConfig.builder()
    .browserConfig { b ->
        b.customSchemes(listOf(
            KromiumCustomScheme.secure("app"),
            KromiumCustomScheme(
                schemeName = "local",
                isStandard = true,
                isLocal = true,
                isSecure = true,
                isCorsEnabled = true,
                isCspBypassing = false,
                isFetchEnabled = true
            )
        ))
    }
    .build()

sections.title: Serving Assets from the Classpath
sections.content: `KromiumSchemeHandler.fromClasspath()` creates a turnkey handler that streams resources bundled inside your application JAR. Supports SPA fallback routing for React/Vue/Angular apps.

sections.title: Serving Assets from a Local Directory
sections.content: `KromiumSchemeHandler.fromDirectory()` serves files from a local filesystem directory with built-in directory traversal protection and SPA fallback support.

codeSnippet.code:
val handler = KromiumSchemeHandler.fromDirectory(
    directory = File("./frontend/dist"),
    spaFallback = "index.html",
    defaultHeaders = mapOf(
        "X-Frame-Options" to "DENY"
    )
)
engine.registerSchemeHandler("app", "myapp", handler)

sections.title: Dynamic Custom Handlers
sections.content: For dynamic content, implement `KromiumAssetHandler` directly. Return `KromiumAssetResponse.json()`, `.html()`, `.text()`, or `.stream()` — or `null` for 404.
